purpose: Separate healthy-run useful-work coverage from replacement latency after an abrupt worker disappearance. Commercial-agent competitiveness requires both.

abrupt_loss_recovery_gap.definition: first meaningful replacement-worker progress minus last meaningful predecessor progress

current_capability.healthy_run: NEAR_PASS; 01:00 window had 852s endpoint coverage but strict substantive gap audit found 125s max vs 120 allowed

actions_schedule_limit: GitHub officially documents a minimum 5-minute schedule interval and warns scheduled workflows can be delayed under load and may even be dropped. Therefore Actions cron is a liveness rescue layer, not a <=120-second fast-recovery mechanism.
interpretation: The hard continuation gate can make a healthy invocation highly utilized, but recovery SLO is separate. A platform-ended invocation can still leave a large gap unless an independent event-driven wake exists. Five-minute Actions cron improves worst-case rescue but cannot satisfy the fast-recovery target by itself.
promotion_rule: Do not call RRuleR SaaS-grade on utilization alone until both three consecutive fixed coverage windows pass under substantive evidence policy and abrupt-loss recovery is demonstrated under an independent wake path.
next_experiment: After an independent Work event consumer is provisioned and write probe passes, simulate a stale owner in the event lab, measure event-to-first-work latency and verify recovery gap <=120 seconds without duplicate substantive execution.
